clue.text: Supposed lad almost made a bid

indicators.note: almost means the word for lad loses its final letter

parts.note: a lad is a son
in bridge, to make a bid is to call, so made a bid is called

explanation.surface: A young man very nearly put in an offer at an auction, or so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SON to SO. In bridge a bid is a call, so 'made a bid' gives CALLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something so-called signals doubt that it deserves the name, which is what supposed conveys.

clue.text: See forceful thrust with foot results in penalty

parts.note: to spot is to see
a kick is a forceful thrust with the foot

explanation.surface: Seeing a player kick out at someone leads to a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot kick is the football term for a penalty kick, taken from the penalty spot.

clue.text: Seat I must sit in daily

indicators.note: must sit in means the letter I is placed inside the word for a cleaner

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British term for a cleaning woman who comes in each day

explanation.surface: Someone insists they must take a seat every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a piece of furniture for sitting on, a kind of seat.

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships

explanation.surface: A boat with a smaller cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed boat used to lighten ships of their cargo; separately it is the comparative of light.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Delicious meals on a holiday retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is an informal word for food or a meal.

indicators.note: heard tells us to use a word that is pronounced the same as the one meaning immediately

parts.note: to go straight there is to go immediately

explanation.surface: Something one hears at once, as a reflex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise, but here it is a narrow channel of sea, as in Plymouth Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of water between two landmasses, and so is a strait.

definitions.meaning: to ... is to deal illegally, as in drug ...
the vehicles moving on a road

explanation.surface: Smuggling in cars and lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means both illegal dealing in goods and the cars and lorries moving along roads.

definitions.note: the 's is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: irritated suggests the letters of the phrase are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A social climber's infrequent visit annoyed the hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parvenu's' reads as 'Parvenu is', so the definition is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart who has risen socially, and arriviste is a near-synonym from French.

clue.text: After short time children's author becomes vulgar

indicators.note: After places the author's name following the letter for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the Rev W. Awdry wrote the Thomas the Tank Engine books for children

explanation.surface: A children's writer turns crude after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rev W. Awdry created Thomas the Tank Engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means showy but cheap and in poor taste, much like vulgar.

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
a range is an open field, as for grazing or a firing range
a tip is a rubbish dump in British usage

explanation.surface: A butterfly flits over a field next to a rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIP is the British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a white European butterfly whose males have orange wingtips, an example of the class.

clue.text: Sweet couple in conversation over fall

indicators.note: in conversation means we take a word spoken like the one for couple

parts.note: a pair is a couple
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A sweet couple talking just before a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear drop is a boiled sweet shaped like a pear and flavoured with pear essence.

indicators.note: about means the letters for a quarrel wrap around the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over who has the right to put down a marker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' also means a crossbow bolt, a sly nod to the answer. 'about' puts R inside A ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign pointing the way, a marker showing direction on a map or signpost.

clue.text: Martial art demonstrated by artist seized by little Katherine

indicators.note: seized by means the letters for the artist are held within the short name

parts.note: Kate is a short form of Katherine
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A young girl called Katherine grabs a painter to show off her fighting moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese unarmed combat discipline, an example of a martial art.

definitions.meaning: A 1925 comedy by the playwright Noel Coward
an allergic reaction to pollen is a complaint, an ailment

explanation.surface: A timid person's job is something to moan about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' is not a scaredy-cat but Noel Coward, the English playwright; a complaint is an ailment, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's title names the pollen allergy, a seasonal ailment, while also being a celebrated stage comedy.

clue.text: Persuasive speech from rector, I recollected, about hospital

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the letter for hospital
recollected, read as re-collected, says the letters are gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman remembers a stirring sermon given at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered; read as re-collected it shuffles RECTOR and I into RETORIC, which 'about' wraps round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking, and also the speech that uses it.

clue.text: Empty the American packs ready for action

parts.note: to clear something is to empty it
Americans call packs of cards decks

explanation.surface: Someone empties the American's bags so they can get going.
explanation.definitionFit: On a warship the decks were cleared before battle, so the idiom means to prepare for action.

definitions.meaning: box is a shrub that keeps its leaves all year

explanation.surface: Produce that stays fresh when kept in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is not a container but the shrub used for hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is a plant that keeps its foliage all year, and figuratively something that never loses freshness.

clue.text: Change, say, before seeing old trusted friend

indicators.note: before places the word for change ahead of the following pieces

parts.note: to alter is to change
eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Someone transforms, say, before meeting an old confidant.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a very close and trusted companion, literally a second self.

parts.note: eight is a number
some means a few
to reel is to rock or sway unsteadily

explanation.surface: A dance tune with a few rock numbers in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests music but is the verb meaning to sway, REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a lively Scottish country dance performed by eight people.

clue.text: A drink in heart of Burgundy, with ten cakes!

indicators.note: in says the a and the drink are placed inside the central letters of the wine region
heart of picks out the central letters of the word

parts.note: tea is a drink
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A tipple in the heart of the French wine region, served with ten pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes GU, the two middle letters of Burgundy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateaux are rich cream cakes, the plural of the French word for cake.

indicators.note: abroad means spread out or astray, so the letters of learnt are scattered

explanation.surface: English learned overseas is never spoken badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' suggests foreign travel, but it means astray, shuffling LEARNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts for ever without interruption, so it is never broken off.

clue.text: Animal coming from mountain, a short cat

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: short means the word cat loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A creature from the mountains: a cat lacking in height.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American domesticated mammal related to the llama.

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters of the designer's name are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: The fashion designer Jean Paul Gaultier has reworked a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like a fashion item, but it means a binding cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is a cord or thread used for binding, as surgeons do to tie off a blood vessel.

definitions.meaning: the eye of a storm is its calm middle
the heart of something is its middle

explanation.surface: Two organs of the body, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the eye of a hurricane and the heart of a city name the middle point of something.

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the wild cat's name

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots

explanation.surface: A wild cat at last notices her newborn kittens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests a brood of kittens; it is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is rubbish, and litter is rubbish dropped in public places.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few folk agree to sign a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request or appeal, just as a petition is.

indicators.note: ringing means the motoring organisation's letters encircle the others

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motorists' organisation
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Drivers phone in about a ground in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests a phone call; it means surrounding. The AA is the UK's Automobile Association, a breakdown service for motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or shows, essentially a synonym for a stadium.

clue.text: Row of trees in area in London somehow protected by church

indicators.note: protected by means the jumbled letters are sheltered within the letters for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of area and London are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: A line of trees in some part of London is sheltered by a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area in London' reads like a district of the city, but both words are just letters to be mixed; 'protected by' then wraps the church round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is usually a row of columns, but by extension it is also a line of trees planted at regular intervals.

clue.text: Wing sounds like an unknown quantity

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: in algebra x is the classic unknown quantity, so this is an x

explanation.surface: A building extension of uncertain size.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the answer is 'an X', and x is the standard unknown quantity in algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building or extension attached to the main one, much like a wing of a house.

clue.text: Everyone taken in by most of band's hype

indicators.note: taken in means the word for everyone is swallowed by the small word that follows

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word for a band

parts.note: a hoop is a band, as round a barrel

explanation.surface: Everyone gets fooled by a pop group's publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a pop group but is a ring, HOOP, cut to HOO by 'most of'. 'by' itself is a piece, holding ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy, extravagant publicity, the same idea as hype.
